subject: non-spatial evaluation of covars with _eval only fails when >1 covar present

messages.author: b74406a12280246a
messages.subject: non-spatial evaluation of covars with _eval only fails when >1 covar present
parts:
I have tried this with the gorillas dataset to make sure it's not an issue with my data or model. When we run a 1 covar model, we can evaluate the effect of the covariate using the suffix _eval in the formula call of the predict function. so, the below code would produce a prediction on the new values provided in the "data" argument

####
library(inlabru)
library(INLA)

data(gorillas, package = "inlabru")
nests <- gorillas$nests
mesh <- gorillas$mesh
boundary <- gorillas$boundary
gcov <- gorillas$gcov

elevation <- gcov$elevation
waterdist <- gcov$waterdist

ecomp <- coordinates ~ elev(elevation, model = "linear") +
  # wd(waterdist, model = "linear") +
  Intercept(1)

efit <- lgcp(ecomp, nests, samplers = boundary, domain = list(coordinates = mesh))

elev.pred <- predict(
  efit,
  data = data.frame(elevation = seq(0, 100, length.out = 1000)),
  formula = ~ elev_eval(elevation)
)
####

However, if I add the water distance component to the formula, and run the model with the two covariates, and then try the predict function, I get the following error

Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘over’ for signature ‘"data.frame", "SpatialPixelsDataFrame"’

Versions:
inlabru version: 2.7.0.9006
INLA version: 23.04.24

Is this expected behaviour? If it is, is there a way that I can evaluate and plot the effect of covariates in a model with multiple covariates?

Many thanks,

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] non-spatial evaluation of covars with _eval only fails when >1 covar present
parts: When you're providing data to predict in a different format than expected by the component definitions, you may need to tell it not to try to evaluate some components. In your case, you're only supplying elevation values, so waterdist cannot be evaluated. Use the include/exclude arguments to predict() to say which components should be involved.
